catalog_quote: 194. Apart from phonemes and their combinations (phonological syntagmata) we have to recognize a prosody or phoneme-attribute in Old Russian, which, as in the modern language, takes the form of stress. This appears to have had phonematic value in both phases of Russian. The examination of modern Russian stress reveals that it is defined by two qualities, viz. it is irregular in incidence and it is mobile in the paradigm ... Old Russian stress can be surmised by the projection of the modern or at least of the 'known' sixteenth-century system into the medieval 'unknown'. ... 378. As we can pursue the accentuation of Russian with some confidence as far back as the fourteenth century, we are led to observe that the earlier type of Russian resembled the modern language in at least three essentials: (a) the dynamic quality of its stress, which makes it different from what we know of stress in…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the Matthews djvu text we hold at the stated sections and pages. (2) The deciding source is a 1960 student historical grammar whose Old Russian stress claim is avowedly a back-projection; the field's authoritative description is Zaliznyak 1985/2014, now downloaded from the publisher-institute's open site. (3) Zaliznyak 2014 pp. 10-11, 28 confirms the lexical classification (no syllable-counting restriction on stress placement; accent is an underivable property of each morpheme; paradigmatic mobility via accent paradigms a/b/c) and refines it: accent-paradigm-c 'enclinomena' were phonologically stressless and took automatic initial prominence on the phonetic word (onto proclitics), stress could not sit on a weak jer, and a rhythmic secondary stress fell on the second post-tonic syllable; autonomous and automatic stress merged c. 14th c. None of this changes kind=l

sources.quote: p. 10: 'In every orthotonic word form phonological stress is fixed to one of its syllables; under no phrasal conditions does it shift or disappear. There are no general restrictions on the place of phonological stress connected with counting syllables from the beginning or end of the word form (cf. ulica, rabota, storona, rakovina, klevetniki, rasskazyvaete...)'; restriction: stress could not fall on a weak jer (retracts one syllable left). Enclinomena (word forms with all syllables phonologically unstressed, accent paradigm c forms) receive an automatic prosodic strengthening of the initial s
sources.locator: Ocherk drevnerusskoj akcentnoj sistemy, sec. 1.2-1.3, pp. 10-11; Prilozhenie sec. 1.10-1.11, pp. 27-28
sources.note: The authoritative synchronic outline of the Old Russian accent system plus a 700-pp accentological dictionary from 14th-17th c. accented manuscripts; our classification rests on a 1960 English student historical grammar that reconstructs stress by projection. Confirms lexical (free, morpheme-marked stress) and adds the enclinomena/automatic-initial default and rhythmic secondary stress that the record's the primary-stress rule lacks.
